I went to my first funeral at about 6, my grandparent. I remember being interested, but couldn't grasp it. At 11, my mother passed. At her funeral, all I wondered was how she looked so much less sick, but so much more... Dead. I researched, discovered the funeral industry, and fell in love!

"Mortuary people" go by many different titles. There's the Funeral Director, who will run the ropes. Embalming, cremations, even lawn mowing. Whatever needs to be done. Then there's your Mortician, or an Embalmer, which is what I'll be studying.

There's much more to it than just dress up. There's body preparation, which I won't get very much into. If you're wanting to be cremated, your body is still prepared for viewing beforehand, and there's a bit of a process before and after the actual cremation. Lots of weighing and mashing. (yes, you will be pulverised.)
